title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Animal and Range Science (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Animal and Range Science (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a method of feed quality evaluation?
questions.explanation: Price of the feed is not a method of feed quality evaluation.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not an energy concentrate:
questions.explanation: Soybean meal is a protein concentrate, not an energy concentrate. It typically contains 44-48% crude protein and is used as a protein supplement in animal diets. The other options (wheat bran, maize bran, and wheat middlings) are energy concentrates with higher carbohydrate content.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is among the major constraints that affect the apiculture sector in Ethiopia?
options: Adequate research works to support development programme
The ideal climatic conditions and the diversity of floral resources
questions.explanation: All of the above are constraints affecting the apiculture sector in Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not correctly matched with dromedary and Bactrian camels characteristics?
options: Dromedary camels > lives in hot arid and semi-arid of Africa and Arabian countries
Bactrian camels > are fewer in numbers than Dromedary
Bactrian camel > have single hump while Dromedary have two humps
Bactrian camels > are numerous in numbers than Dromedary
questions.explanation: Bactrian camels are not more numerous than Dromedary camels.

questions.questionText: Which is true regarding Newcastle disease?
options: Treatment and control method is possible
questions.explanation: Newcastle disease is transmitted through infected droppings (A) and is caused by a paramyxovirus (B). It is a highly contagious viral disease affecting birds, particularly poultry. While there is no specific treatment for the virus itself, control methods include vaccination, biosecurity measures, and proper management practices.

questions.questionText: All are kinds of Green succulent roughage except:
questions.explanation: Straw is not considered a green succulent roughage.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diseases occurs within 72 hours of calving in high yielding cows?
questions.explanation: Milk fever (hypocalcemia) occurs within 72 hours of calving in high yielding dairy cows due to calcium mobilization for milk production. It's characterized by low blood calcium levels causing muscle weakness, paralysis and potentially death if untreated.

questions.questionText: Of the following, what are the causes of erosion or extinction of animal genetic resources?
questions.explanation: All listed options contribute to the erosion or extinction of animal genetic resources.

questions.questionText: _____________________ is controlled and coordinated by gonadotrophin hormones, LH, FSH, and Testosterone.
questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis (sperm production) is controlled by gonadotropic hormones. FSH stimulates Sertoli cells to support sperm development, LH stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone, and testosterone promotes spermatogenesis and development of secondary sexual characteristics in males.

questions.questionText: Which of animal feed refers to all those feeds that have not been traditionally used in animal feeding?
questions.explanation: Non-conventional feed refers to feeds that have not been traditionally used in animal feeding.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an advantage of raising sheep and goats?
options: Adapted to different climates and production systems
questions.explanation: Both options A and B are advantages of raising sheep and goats.

questions.questionText: Grasses, legumes, forages, succulents, and greens are best in nutritive value either at:
questions.explanation: Grasses, legumes, forages, succulents, and greens are best in nutritive value at all stages.

questions.questionText: The fat deposits in the carcass are filled in the order, from first to last:
options: Subcutaneous, internal, intermuscular, and intramuscular fat
Internal, subcutaneous, intramuscular, and intermuscular fat
Internal, intermuscular, subcutaneous, and intramuscular fat
Intramuscular, subcutaneous, intermuscular, and internal fat
questions.explanation: The correct order of fat deposits in the carcass is subcutaneous, internal, intermuscular, and intramuscular fat.

questions.questionText: Among the following, one is not true about vitamin A:
options: Required in a very small amount in the daily ration of the animal
Can be prepared by the body from the feed consumed
Can be both fat soluble and fat soluble at a time
questions.explanation: Vitamin A cannot be both fat soluble and water soluble at the same time; it is exclusively a fat-soluble vitamin.

questions.questionText: Why do farmers castrate their male sheep and goats?
options: To increase body size growth rate
For extra muscle development and fat accumulation
To cull the animal because of defects
questions.explanation: Farmers castrate male sheep and goats for all the listed reasons.

questions.questionText: During ration formulation, the following information is very essential except:
options: Feeding standard of an animal in trial
questions.explanation: Morphology of an animal is not essential information during ration formulation.

questions.questionText: __________________ gene action the phenotype of the heterozygous possess surpasses either of the phenotype produced by the two homozygous parents.
questions.explanation: Over dominance (also called heterosis or hybrid vigor) is when the phenotype of heterozygous individuals surpasses either homozygous parent. This results in offspring with superior qualities compared to either parent and is an important concept in breeding programs.

questions.questionText: A type of chromosome rearrangement is a ____________, in which a chromosome segment is inverted — turned 180 degrees.
questions.explanation: Chromosome inversion is when a chromosome segment is inverted.

questions.questionText: Of the following, one is not a honeybee product.
questions.explanation: Nectar is not a honeybee product.

questions.questionText: Considering the current situation, sheep and goat production and productivity in Ethiopia is constrained by:
questions.explanation: All listed factors constrain sheep and goat production in Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: Let's assume 200kg of feed is needed to feed 2kg egg-laying birds, a feeding standard shows that a 16% crude protein ration is needed. Corn and Soybean oil meal (SBOM) are selected as feeds. A feed composition shows that corn has 8.9% and SBOM has 45.8% crude protein. How much corn and soybean oil meal need to be mixed together for 200 kg of feed? Which is correct regarding the above sentences?
options: 161.6 kg of corn needed in the mix
38.4 kg of SBM needed in the mix
questions.explanation: Using the Pearson square method: (45.8-16)=29.8 parts corn and (16-8.9)=7.1 parts SBOM. Total parts: 36.9. Therefore, corn needed = (29.8/36.9)×200 = 161.6 kg, and SBOM needed = (7.1/36.9)×200 = 38.4 kg. Both A and B are correct.

questions.questionText: Which one is odd about feed digestive anatomy in farm animals?
questions.explanation: Sensory organ is not directly involved in feed digestion.

questions.questionText: Oversowing should be promoted in areas:
questions.explanation: Oversowing can be promoted in all listed areas.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following are main characteristics of beef breed?
questions.explanation: All listed options are main characteristics of beef breeds.

questions.questionText: In which of the following mating types of animal are the percentages of heterozygosity higher?
questions.explanation: Outcrossing results in higher percentages of heterozygosity compared to inbreeding methods. Outcrossing involves mating unrelated animals within the same breed, increasing genetic diversity and heterozygosity. This reduces the expression of harmful recessive alleles and often leads to improved fitness and performance.

questions.questionText: From the following alternatives, which one is not correct?
options: DNA has a highly ordered structure
+ G = T + C or purines = pyrimidine
DNA is more stable than RNA
questions.explanation: The statement 'A + G = T + C or purines = pyrimidine' is incorrect. While A pairs with T and G pairs with C in DNA, there's no guarantee that the total number of purines (A+G) equals the total number of pyrimidines (T+C) in any given DNA segment, except in double-stranded DNA.

questions.questionText: Sheep and goat farm records enable the manager or owner:
options: To plan future direction of the farm
questions.explanation: All listed options are benefits of maintaining farm records.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the cock reproductive organ?
questions.explanation: All options except the uterus are part of the cock's reproductive system.

questions.questionText: Of the following, one is a wrong statement.
options: All castes of honeybees collect nectar and pollen from plants
Pollen collecting honeybees are good pollinators than nectar gatherers
Avoid spraying of pesticides while crop is in blooming and honeybees are visiting to it
Honeybees cause no damage to the crops
questions.explanation: Not all castes of honeybees collect nectar and pollen. Only worker bees forage for nectar and pollen, while queen bees and drones do not collect these resources.

questions.questionText: ___________________ is the site of sperm production in the testis.
questions.explanation: Seminiferous tubules are the site of spermatogenesis (sperm production) in the testes. Leydig cells produce testosterone but don't produce sperm. Tunica dartos is a muscle layer in the scrotum, and cremaster muscle regulates testicular temperature by moving the testes closer to or farther from the body.

questions.questionText: The signs of the first stage of calving composed of:
options: Cow tending to bellow and restless
questions.explanation: All listed signs are indicative of the first stage of calving.

questions.questionText: The following is/are considered as Tropical grass except:
questions.explanation: Medicago scutellata is not considered a tropical grass.

questions.questionText: Of the following, which is not part of the chicken oviduct?
questions.explanation: The ovary is not part of the chicken oviduct.

questions.questionText: One is not part of the male accessory sex organs:
questions.explanation: The cervix is not part of the male accessory sex organs.

questions.questionText: Hormones of reproduction originate from:
questions.explanation: Reproductive hormones originate from all three sources: the hypothalamus (GnRH), pituitary (FSH, LH), and gonads (testosterone, estrogen, progesterone). These work together in the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis to regulate reproductive functions including gametogenesis, sexual behavior, and pregnancy.

questions.questionText: One of the following is correct about optimum temperature of air type incubator.
questions.explanation: The optimum temperature for an air type incubator is 37.2 to 38.2°C.

questions.questionText: The multiple effects of a single gene on the phenotype of an organism is called ___________.
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy refers to when a single gene affects multiple, seemingly unrelated phenotypic traits. This occurs because the gene product may function in different cells or tissues, or affect multiple metabolic pathways. Classic examples include phenylketonuria and Marfan syndrome in humans.

questions.questionText: ______________ contains blood vessels and it brings blood vessels to chorion.
questions.explanation: The allantois contains blood vessels that connect to the chorion.

questions.questionText: One of the following is false about the advantages of deep litter chicken house.
options: Production is higher because birds are kept under hygienic conditions.
questions.explanation: None of the statements are false; all are advantages of deep litter chicken houses.

questions.questionText: _______________________ is the process of forming different kinds of cells from similar cells of the early embryo.
questions.explanation: Differentiation is the process by which cells in the early embryo develop into specialized cell types with specific functions. This process involves selective gene expression where some genes are activated while others are repressed, leading to the formation of different tissues and organs during embryonic development.

questions.questionText: In Ethiopia, more than half proportion of beef comes from:
options: Old oxen kept for draft purposes
questions.explanation: All listed options contribute to the beef supply in Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: The important pasture management practices that yield maximum forage production in Ethiopia are:
questions.explanation: All listed practices are important for maximum forage production.

questions.questionText: Which is correct regarding the recommended space requirement per bird for egg-laying birds?
questions.explanation: Both A and B are correct regarding space requirements.

questions.questionText: Depending on the type of feed used, a fattening period ranging from ____ to _____ is enough for finishing cattle.
questions.explanation: A fattening period of 6 to 9 months is typically sufficient for finishing cattle. This duration allows adequate time for muscle development and fat deposition. The actual length depends on factors such as the animal's initial condition, breed, age, feed quality, and target market specifications.

questions.questionText: ______________ genes which result in viability reduction of individuals or become a cause for death of individuals carrying them.
questions.explanation: Lethal genes can reduce viability or cause death in individuals carrying them.

questions.questionText: All are factors affecting pasture improvement except one:
questions.explanation: The unavailability of nutrients is actually a factor affecting pasture improvement, not an exception. The presence of nutrients is essential for improved pasture growth and quality.

questions.questionText: Which is true regarding round feeder for 8 - 18 week age of birds, the diameter of the material is 35cm?
questions.explanation: The correct number of birds per round feeder is 27.

questions.questionText: __________________ is used to measure the temperature that is in the thawing unit to warm straw.
questions.explanation: A thermometer is used to measure the temperature in the thawing unit when warming semen straws. Maintaining the precise temperature (typically 35-37°C) is critical for semen viability, as improper thawing temperatures can damage sperm cells and reduce fertility rates.

questions.questionText: ______________ arises from hybridization between two species; the resulting polyploid carries chromosome sets derived from two or more species.
questions.explanation: Allopolyploidy arises from hybridization between two different species followed by chromosome doubling. The resulting organism contains chromosome sets from both parent species. This is common in plant breeding and evolution, creating fertile hybrids with unique characteristics such as seen in wheat (Triticum) and cotton (Gossypium).

questions.questionText: _________________ refers to the synthesis of milk by the epithelial cells and the passage of milk from the cytoplasm of the cells into the alveolar lumen.
questions.explanation: Milk secretion refers to the synthesis and passage of milk into the alveolar lumen.

questions.questionText: Role of Females includes except:
questions.explanation: Sperm production is not a role of females.

questions.questionText: Parameters which are not considered during selection of milking goats are/is:
questions.explanation: All the listed parameters (horn, body shape, and udder structure) are considered during selection of milking goats. The udder structure directly affects milk production capacity and milking ease, while body conformation and horn type are related to breed standards and management considerations.

questions.questionText: Assume that your family has a production farm and you are assigned to clean the goat house or shed every two days, so what is your view?
options: Accept for the sake of family request
Consider as a way of livelihood and fully involved in the farm operation
As the farm has an unpleasant smell, refuse to do so
I never participate in any livestock farm
questions.explanation: Considering it as a way of livelihood and being involved is a positive view.

questions.questionText: Choose the sex-influenced trait:
questions.explanation: Pattern baldness is a classic sex-influenced trait. It is controlled by autosomal genes but is influenced by sex hormones, typically expressed more in males due to testosterone levels. Hypertrichosis is not specifically sex-influenced.

questions.questionText: Among the following honeybee species, one is predominantly found in Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: Apis mellifera is predominantly found in Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: _____________ is used to pick up the semen when in the tank and thawing unit.
questions.explanation: Straw tweezers are used to pick up the semen.

questions.questionText: Which one is an on-farm sheep and goat meat product quality determinant?
questions.explanation: All listed options are determinants of meat product quality.

questions.questionText: ____________ is the replacement or re-growth of lost or damaged body parts.
questions.explanation: Regeneration is the biological process of replacing or restoring lost or damaged body parts. It varies among species - some can regenerate entire limbs or organs while others have limited regenerative capacity. This process involves cell proliferation, differentiation, and tissue remodeling to restore structure and function.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about protein quality in terms of amino acid balance?
options: Plant source protein is more preferable than animal source
Animal source protein is more preferable than plant source
Roots and tubers source protein are more preferable than animal source
Microbial protein is more economical than plant source
questions.explanation: Animal source protein is generally more preferable due to its amino acid profile.

questions.questionText: Assume the breeder wants to purchase animals from the market for breeding. Which of the following types of selection should he/she use?
questions.explanation: Pedigree selection is often used for purchasing breeding animals.

questions.questionText: Among the following, one is the advantage of rearing honeybees in movable-frame hive?
options: Pure honey can be extracted by damaging the combs
Higher amount of honeybees' wax can be produced than a top-bar hive
high degree of craftsmanship is required
Facilitates in regular and easy inspection of colonies
questions.explanation: Movable-frame hives facilitate regular and easy inspection of colonies.

questions.questionText: One is not necessarily a source of protein but a source of nitrogen for non-ruminant animals:
questions.explanation: Poultry litters are a source of nitrogen but not a direct source of protein.

questions.questionText: Which types of grass species are planted by vegetative parts, especially by stem cuttings?
questions.explanation: Elephant grass (Pennisetum purpureum) is typically propagated by vegetative parts, especially stem cuttings. Cenchrus ciliaris is more commonly established by seed.

questions.questionText: Among the following, one is an example of good traits of a colony that honeybee breeders should consider:
questions.explanation: Good temperament is a desirable trait in honeybee colonies.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true about why nutritionists worry about feed standards?
options: Feed requirement is directly influenced by the price of feed
Feed standard is directly related to feed type
Feed requirement is influenced by the breed of animal
Standard feed recommendation is directly related to production level
questions.explanation: While price influences feed choice, it does not directly relate to feed standards.

questions.questionText: Camel is first originated in __________________ country?
questions.explanation: Camels first originated in North America during the Eocene period, about 40-45 million years ago, not in a specific country. They later spread to South America and Asia, becoming extinct in North America. The two main types today (dromedary and Bactrian) evolved in Asia and the Middle East.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following hormone/s is/are essential for the maintenance as well as initiation of lactation?
questions.explanation: All listed hormones are essential for lactation. Prolactin is responsible for milk production, oxytocin facilitates milk ejection or let-down, and adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulates cortisol production which helps regulate metabolism during lactation. These hormones work together to maintain the lactation process.

questions.questionText: Which one is bloodless castration of male sheep and goats?
questions.explanation: Elastrator is a method of bloodless castration.

questions.questionText: During semen processing, one is not considered as a selection parameter for semen storage in liquid nitrogen tank at -196°C.
questions.explanation: Semen color is not a critical parameter for selection.

questions.questionText: Mention the common sheep and goat production farm routine management practices:
questions.explanation: All listed practices are common management practices.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not part of the livestock feed classification?
options: Can be grouped into roughage and concentrate
Can be protein and energy concentrate and bulky feed
questions.explanation: Digestibility and palatability are not part of feed classification.

questions.questionText: The vital physiological functions such as breathing, keeping constant body temperature, and repair of damaged tissues are satisfied through:
questions.explanation: Maintenance ration satisfies vital physiological functions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following metabolic disorders is mainly common in grazing-based animal feeding?
questions.explanation: Hypomagnesemia (grass tetany) is most common in grazing-based animal feeding, particularly in cattle grazing on lush, rapidly growing pastures that are low in magnesium. Hypocalcemia (milk fever) is more associated with dairy cattle around calving.

questions.questionText: Is an essential plant nutrient that is central to protein formation, photosynthesis, and other key plant functions.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is an essential plant nutrient crucial for protein formation (as it is a component of amino acids), chlorophyll synthesis (affecting photosynthesis), nucleic acid production, and overall plant growth. Nitrogen deficiency typically results in yellowing of older leaves (chlorosis) and stunted growth in plants.

questions.questionText: One of the following is a meat type of breed.
questions.explanation: Both Babcock and Bovans Brown are meat-type breeds.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is/are true about the diestrum phase?
options: The phase may last 1 to 5 days
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum is fully grown during the diestrum phase.

questions.questionText: One of the following is true about lipids:
options: Contain nitrogen and phosphorus in their structure with protein
Required in a very small amount in the daily ration of the animal
Can be both fat soluble and fat soluble at a time
questions.explanation: Lipids are required in relatively small amounts in animal diets compared to other macronutrients like carbohydrates, though they are not micronutrients. They provide essential fatty acids and serve as carriers for fat-soluble vitamins.

questions.questionText: _________________ is the observable or measurable characteristics (called traits) of that organism.
questions.explanation: Phenotype refers to the observable or measurable characteristics of an organism, resulting from the interaction between genotype and environment. This includes physical traits, physiological properties, behaviors, and other measurable qualities that can be observed externally.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a constraint of camel production in Ethiopia:
questions.explanation: Favorable climatic conditions are not a constraint for camel production.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not necessarily true with regard to factors governing the distribution of camels?
options: Mode of living of people affects camel distribution
Cultural and religious taboos affect camel distribution
Climatic factor can affect camel distribution
Economic factor cannot affect camel distribution
questions.explanation: Economic factors can indeed affect camel distribution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered to play a substantial role as the primary feed resource throughout the wet season in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Natural pasture plays a substantial role as the primary feed resource during the wet season in Ethiopia. During this period, rangelands and grasslands flourish with nutritious vegetation due to rainfall, providing abundant grazing opportunities for livestock before becoming scarce in the dry season.

questions.questionText: Which is true regarding one meter long feeder for 0 - 8 week age of birds?
questions.explanation: The correct number of birds per long feeder is 27.

questions.questionText: __________________ are present in the autosomes but their expression is determined by the presence or absence of one of the sex-hormones.
questions.explanation: Sex influenced inheritance refers to traits whose expression is affected by sex hormones.

questions.questionText: ________________ occurs when an area around the esophagus is stimulated with coarse material (scratch effect of fibrous roughages).
questions.explanation: Regurgitation occurs when coarse material stimulates the area around the esophagus.

questions.questionText: Why do we need to crossbreed indigenous sheep and goat breeds with exotic breeds?
options: To compete with developed nations' sheep population
questions.explanation: Crossbreeding aims to increase productivity.

questions.questionText: In practical animal feeding, it is advisable to mix:
options: 85 - 90% of plant proteins with 10 - 15% animal proteins
0% plant proteins with 30% oil seed cake proteins
questions.explanation: Mixing plant and animal proteins in the specified ratios is advisable.

questions.questionText: When honey is stored in the honey sac, it is mixed with:
options: Water to make the nectar less viscous
Preservative to keep honey for a long time
Enzymes for the production of fructose and glucose
questions.explanation: When honeybees collect nectar, it's stored in their honey sac (crop) where it mixes with enzymes like invertase (sucrase) that begin converting nectar's sucrose into the simple sugars fructose and glucose. This enzymatic process continues after bees deposit the nectar in hive cells, eventually transforming it into honey.

questions.questionText: Which is a method of developing an embryo into a chick within the shell up to hatching time?
questions.explanation: Both incubation and natural incubation are methods for developing an embryo into a chick.

questions.questionText: Functions of the epididymis include except:
questions.explanation: The epididymis does not produce hormones.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not critically needed in ration formulation?
options: Preparation of nutritionally-complete diets for feeding animals
questions.explanation: Minimum ingredient cost is not critically needed in ration formulation.

questions.questionText: ______________ method involves an electrical probe to collect semen from the male animals.
questions.explanation: Electro-ejaculation involves using an electrical probe to collect semen.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a physiological adaptation of camels that allows them to withstand long periods of time without any external source of water?
options: Ability to reduce fecal and urine water loss
questions.explanation: Releasing bad smell is not a physiological adaptation related to water conservation in camels. The other options are genuine adaptations that help camels survive in arid environments with limited water access.

questions.questionText: Function of the placenta includes:
questions.explanation: The placenta's primary function is nutrient exchange between mother and fetus. It also facilitates gas exchange (rather than blocking it), waste removal, hormone production, and provides immunological protection. The answer cannot be 'All of the above' because the placenta facilitates rather than blocks gas exchange.

questions.questionText: Which is a process in which a bright light is shone through an egg to enable identifying defects?
questions.explanation: Candling is the process used to identify defects in eggs.

questions.questionText: All are the general mineral functions except:
questions.explanation: Energy synthesis is not a primary function of minerals. Minerals are typically involved in structural components, enzyme activation, acid-base balance, osmotic pressure regulation, and oxygen transport, but energy production is primarily the role of macronutrients (carbohydrates, fats, proteins).

questions.questionText: Beef production in Ethiopia is low due to all except ___:
questions.explanation: Shorter calving intervals do not contribute to low beef production.

questions.questionText: Factors affecting the expression of estrous behavior in animals are:
questions.explanation: All listed factors can affect estrous behavior.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a property of fats:
questions.explanation: Iodization is not a property of fats. It refers to the addition of iodine to substances (like salt) and is not an inherent property of fats. The presence of double bonds (saturation level), melting point, and solubility are all properties of fats.

questions.questionText: A trisomic person has ______________ chromosomes.
questions.explanation: A trisomic person has 47 chromosomes, which is one more than the normal human diploid number of 46. Trisomy occurs when there are three copies of a particular chromosome instead of the normal two copies, as seen in conditions like Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Edwards syndrome (trisomy 18), or Patau syndrome (trisomy 13).

questions.questionText: How much maize grains will be mixed with cottonseed cake containing 10% and 19% DCP respectively to prepare a 400 kg mixture of 16% DCP?
questions.explanation: 233.34 kg of maize grains is needed to achieve the desired DCP.
